descriptionChirho: The basic Qal active meaning of committing sin or transgression against God or moral law; all person/number/gender/tense inflections of the Qal finite verb and infinitive share this core sense, evidenced by consistent Arabic أَخْطَأَ/خَطِئَ (to err/sin), Korean 죄를 범하다 (to commit sin), Swahili kutenda dhambi (to commit sin), Spanish pecar (to sin), and Hindi पाप करना (to sin).

The Qal participle used substantivally to denote 'the sinner' or 'one who sins' as a noun, distinguished from the verbal participle by syntactic context and consistent Arabic خَاطِئٌ/الْخَاطِئُ (the sinner, nominal form), Korean 죄인 (sinner, noun), Swahili mwenye dhambi (one with sin, nominal), and Spanish pecador (sinner, noun).

The Qal participle used verbally to describe the ongoing act of sinning, distinguished from the substantival use by verbal syntax; Arabic خَاطِئٌ/خَاطِئَةٌ in predicate use, Korean 죄를 짓는 (sin-committing, verbal modifier), Swahili anafanya dhambi / lenye dhambi (committing sin), Spanish peca/pecadora/pecando (verbal sinning).

The original concrete Qal sense of missing a target or failing to reach a mark, distinct from the moral 'sin' sense; evidenced by English 'miss', Spanish 'erraban/faltarás', Korean 빗나가다 (to go astray/miss) vs. the usual 범하다 (to commit), and Swahili shabaha (target-related) rather than dhambi (sin).

The Hifil causative meaning 'to cause/lead someone to sin', a distinct semantic role from the Qal; Arabic جَعَلَ يَخْطَأُ (caused to sin), Korean 범하게 하다 (caused to commit), Swahili kuwakosesha/kuwafanya kutenda dhambi (to make them sin), Spanish hizo pecar/hacer pecar (made to sin).

labelChirho: Hifil participle: one who causes sin
descriptionChirho: The Hifil participle used substantivally for agents who cause others to sin; English 'those making a man [an offender]', Arabic الْمُخْطِئِينَ إِنْسَانًا (those causing a person to sin), Korean 범죄하게 하는 자들이 (those who cause to sin), Swahili wanaowafanya watu kutenda dhambi (those who make people sin).

The Piel factitive/denominative meaning 'to purify, cleanse from sin, make a sin offering for', a ritual/cultic sense distinct from the Qal; Arabic طَهَّرَ (to purify/cleanse), Korean 정결하게 하다 (to make pure/clean), Swahili kutakasa/kufanya upatanisho (to purify/make atonement), Spanish purificar (to purify).

A rare Piel sense meaning 'to bear the loss of, to forfeit', attested in a commercial/legal context (Gen 31:39); English 'bore loss of it', Spanish 'expiaba la', Arabic أُكَفِّرُ ها (I atone/compensate for it), Korean 보상했다 그것을 (compensated for it), distinct from the ritual purification Piel.

The Hitpael reflexive meaning 'to purify oneself, undergo purification', the reflexive counterpart of the Piel purification sense; Arabic يَتَطَهَّرُ (to purify oneself), Korean 정결하게 하다/정결해지다 (to become pure), Swahili kujitakasa (to purify oneself), Spanish purificarse (to purify oneself).
